answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because ocean only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, crystal is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any anchor approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
